description: Reference data describing the major subsystems of the original Java jCRPG engine, and how each is planned to be reimplemented for the web. Loaded at runtime by game_static_core.js.

systems.name: World & Simulation
systems.description: Owns the persistent game world: geography/boundaries, political and economic simulation, climate, world generation and time-of-day/calendar progression. Drives NPC AI at the world scale.

webPort.approach: Pure data + logic port, no rendering dependency. Reimplement as plain JS/TS classes operating on JSON world data.

systems.name: Space Partitioning (Cube Grid)
systems.description: Defines the voxel-like cube/tile grid used to lay out the 3D world: each Cube has typed Sides (wall, floor, ceiling, ramp, etc.) interpreted by CubeInterpreter to build renderable geometry.

webPort.approach: Represent cubes as flat typed arrays (Int8Array/Uint8Array) keyed by grid coordinates; a CubeInterpreter equivalent module derives mesh/side data for the WebGL renderer.

systems.name: 3D Rendering Engine
systems.description: The rendering and scene-graph layer: loads 3D models/terrain tiles, manages pooled/instanced nodes for performance, handles vegetation, lighting, and per-frame scene updates.

webPort.approach: Original engine is built on Ardor3D/JME2 scene graphs rendering via LWJGL/OpenGL. Replace with three.js (WebGL) scene graph: Object3D hierarchy in place of jME/Ardor3D nodes, GLTF/custom loaders in place of ModelLoader.

systems.name: Audio
systems.description: Manages sound channels and playback of effects/music tied to world and UI events.

webPort.approach: Original uses LWJGL's OpenAL bindings. Replace with the Web Audio API (AudioContext, GainNode per channel).

systems.name: Game Logic & Rules
systems.description: Turn-based RPG rules engine: character creation, encounters/combat resolution, scenario scripting and world triggers, plus the top-level mutable game state container.

webPort.approach: Pure logic, no native dependency; port directly to JS as a rules/state-machine module driven by the same static data tables.

systems.name: Objects & Items
systems.description: Data model for equipment, weapons, armor, potions, crafting materials and magical items, plus inventory list handling.

webPort.approach: Almost entirely data-driven; item definitions belong in static_core_data.json (or a dedicated items JSON) with thin JS wrapper classes for instance state (durability, enchantments, stack counts).

systems.name: UI System
systems.description: Custom in-3D-scene UI: HUD overlays, windows/dialogs, meters (health/mana bars), minimap, and text/font rendering, all drawn as part of the 3D scene rather than native OS widgets.
javaLibraries: ardor3d/jme2 (UI drawn via the 3D scene graph)

webPort.approach: Replace in-scene 3D UI nodes with standard DOM/CSS overlays (or a canvas 2D layer) positioned above the WebGL canvas; keeps text crisp and simplifies input handling.

systems.name: Persistence (Save/Load)
systems.description: Serializes/deserializes full game state to disk (see save/ directory) so games can be resumed later.

webPort.approach: Original serializes Java objects to XML via XStream. Replace with JSON.stringify/parse of the JS game-state object, persisted to localStorage/IndexedDB.

systems.name: State Change Abstraction
systems.description: Cross-cutting abstraction layer used to propagate state-change events between world/game logic and the systems that react to them (UI, rendering, AI).

webPort.approach: Model as a lightweight JS EventTarget/pub-sub bus shared across world_state, game_logic, render_engine and ui_overlay modules.
